The chart is a bar graph that compares the perplexity of two different methods, "Per-Output" and "Per-Layer", across various sparsity rates. The x-axis represents the sparsity rate, ranging from 10% to 80% in increments of 10%, while the y-axis represents perplexity on a logarithmic scale from 10^1 to 10^3. The "Per-Output" data series is depicted in blue, and the "Per-Layer" series is shown in orange. The graph shows that as the sparsity rate increases, the perplexity of both methods also increases, with "Per-Layer" having a higher perplexity than "Per-Output" at higher sparsity rates. Notably, the perplexity remains relatively low for both methods until a sparsity rate of 60%, after which it increases more sharply, with "Per-Layer" at 70% sparsity rate having a perplexity around 10^2 and "Per-Output" having a perplexity around 10^1, and at 80% sparsity rate, both methods have perplexity values exceeding 10^2, with "Per-Layer" being slightly higher. The bars are grouped by sparsity rate, allowing for direct comparison between the two methods at each rate.
